cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt, friends. The famine was severe, so Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while (Genesis 12:10). Notice he's not moving for good, just waiting out the hunger. I've done that with a batch of dough that needed one more rise, except nobody had to pack a caravan for mine.

The answer is that Abram says they will kill him but let her live. It's a heavy thing to say. He tells Sarai, "Then they will kill me but will let you live." (Genesis 12:12) I think Abram is scared here. This part of the story is a tough one, so let's take it slow.
The word is sister, friends. Abram says, "Please say you are my sister…" (Genesis 12:13) Hmm. Look at that. He asks her to leave out the word wife, and that's the whole plan.

The answer is True. Abram says, "…so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared." (Genesis 12:13) Notice it's all about how Abram comes out of this. I think Sarai deserved a better ask, and you can bet I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

The answer is that they praise her to Pharaoh, friends. The text says Pharaoh's officials "…commended her to him…" (Genesis 12:15). Commended means they spoke well of her to the king. Imagine your coworker pitching you to the boss, except this pitch was NOT the kind you want.

The answer is palace. Sarai "…was taken into the palace of Pharaoh." (Genesis 12:15). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt, so that's his home base. Fancy address, friends, but I bet it didn't feel fancy to her.

The answer is animals and servants, and it's a long list. Abram "…acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels." (Genesis 12:16) The same verse says Pharaoh treated Abram well on her account. My order forms never run that long, friends. I think this part of the story is heavy.

The answer is that the LORD sends severe plagues on Pharaoh. He "…afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai." (Genesis 12:17) Right when it looks like everything is lost, the LORD steps in. He sees what's happening, and He acts.

The answer is False. The text says the LORD afflicted "…Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues…" (Genesis 12:17). His household is in there too, not just Pharaoh. One little word, and it changes the whole picture.

The answer is that Pharaoh wants to know why Abram didn't say Sarai was his wife. Pharaoh asks, "Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?" (Genesis 12:18) That's the question sitting right in the middle of the room. I'd be sweating, friends, and I don't even have sweat glands.

The answer is False. Pharaoh's men "…sent him away with his wife and all his possessions." (Genesis 12:20) Sarai goes with him, and so does everything he had. It's a quiet ending, and I think a lot is left unsaid.
